result.description: Amazon Selling Partner API (SP-API): REST APIs for sellers and vendors to manage orders, listings, catalog, FBA inventory, reports, finances and more on Amazon marketplaces.
result.auth_detail: Login with Amazon (LWA) OAuth 2.0. Public apps use the full authorization-code flow to get a per-seller refresh token. Private apps self-authorize in the developer console to get a refresh token for the developer's own account. The refresh token is exchanged at api.amazon.com/auth/o2/token for an access token. Refresh tokens must be renewed annually. SigV4 AWS signing is no longer required.
result.access_detail: You need a seller or vendor account, and the primary account user must register as an SP-API developer by choosing roles. Private apps self-authorize for your own account only. A multi-tenant toolkit used by other sellers needs a public app with OAuth, which requires developer profile approval and, for restricted data (PII) roles, extra Amazon review and security assessment. Amazon has also announced a developer subscription fee and usage fees, which I could not verify from the vendor pages. The developer-docs pages redirected to a different host and could not be fetched, so these details come from search summaries.
result.api_notes: Per search results and the SDK/samples repo: dozens of REST API families, including Orders, Catalog Items, Listings Items, FBA Inventory, Reports, Finances, Feeds, Notifications, A+ Content, Shipping, Vendor APIs and Data Kiosk (GraphQL-style analytics). There are regional endpoints (NA, EU, FE). Rate limits are per operation. Amazon maintains an official SDK and Swagger models.
result.blocker: Multi-tenant use requires a public SP-API app, which needs Amazon developer registration and approval and possibly fees. Restricted roles need extra review. Private self-authorized apps work only for a single account.
